description.html: The pirate skull is an aquarium decoration with plenty of character: it wears a dark red pirate bandana, a black patch over one eye and green details that resemble moss and algae, as if it had lain on the seabed for a long time. Fish can swim in and out through the openings, including the large eye socket.

The interior serves as a hiding place for smaller and shyer fish, for whom a place to retreat reduces stress. The skull goes perfectly with a pirate ship, an anchor and shipwrecks, so it is easy to build a complete pirate or nautical aquarium around it, a favorite with kids.

Before putting it in the aquarium, rinse the skull in lukewarm water, without soap or detergents. Set it firmly on sand or gravel with the openings facing the front glass so you can watch fish swim through it. Make sure the openings are large enough for the fish you keep so they cannot get stuck. When cleaning the aquarium, remove algae from the surface with a soft brush. Take a look at our aquariums as well.
